headline_hook: Anthropic Ships Claude for Classrooms While a Cursor Zero-Day Shakes Dev Tooling
preview_topics: Claude's push into education and healthcare
a Cursor zero-day and responsible disclosure failure
the shift from building agents to building agent systems

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The Cursor zero-day reveals that AI code editors' deepest feature — full codebase access — is also their biggest liability, and the industry has no playbook for securing tools that sit between your repo and a language model.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's Ternary-Bonsai-27B release shows a model squeezed to just three weight values (-1, 0, +1). Understanding how ternary quantization preserves model quality while slashing memory by ~10x explains why edge deployment of large models is suddenly viable.

items.title: Claude Gets a Classroom: Anthropic Launches Purpose-Built Teacher Experience
items.angle: This isn't another chatbot wrapper — Anthropic built a dedicated educator product, signaling that vertical-specific AI experiences are the next battleground after generic assistants plateau.
items.key_fact: Purpose-built Claude experience for educators, not a feature flag on the existing product

items.title: HIPAA on Claude Is Now Self-Serve — No Sales Call Required
items.angle: Healthcare teams can now enable HIPAA compliance with a checkbox instead of a multi-week sales process — removing the single biggest friction point for regulated industry adoption.
items.key_fact: Admins can review BAA, download implementation guide, and enable HIPAA compliance without contacting sales

items.title: Google and AIM Deploy Gemini-Powered AI Across India's Tinkering Labs
items.angle: ATL Saathi puts a Gemini-powered teaching tool in front of Indian students learning robotics — a concrete bet that frontier models can work in low-resource education settings at national scale.
items.key_fact: Deployed across India's Atal Tinkering Labs network with AIM partnership

items.title: A Cursor Zero-Day Goes Public After Responsible Disclosure Fails
items.angle: A security firm drops a Cursor zero-day via full disclosure after the company failed to respond — the attack surface in AI coding tools is real, growing, and apparently under-resourced on the vendor side.
items.key_fact: Full disclosure after responsible disclosure process failed; 215 HN upvotes

items.title: AI Engineer World's Fair Recap: The Industry Shifted From Agents to Agent Systems
items.angle: Latent Space distills five defining trends from the conference — the key shift is that teams are no longer building individual agents but designing the orchestration, evaluation, and guardrail systems around them.
items.key_fact: Five macro trends identified; 'agent systems' framing replaces 'agent building'

items.title: Codex Hits 7M Users — Up 10x in Six Months, Adding 1M Per Day
items.angle: Hard usage numbers for the agentic coding race finally surface, and the growth curve is staggering — but Latent Space notes Claude Code's conspicuous silence on its own metrics.
items.key_fact: 7M users, 10x growth in 6 months, +1M in a single day

items.title: Anthropic Commits $10M to Canadian AI Research
items.angle: A $10M commitment to Canadian institutions like MILA and Vector — Anthropic is building academic pipelines outside the US, likely to secure both talent and policy goodwill.

items.title: Claude Code Ships Three Releases: Screen Reader Mode, Live Timers, Worktree Fixes
items.angle: Three rapid-fire releases in a week — the standout additions are accessibility (screen reader mode, vim remaps) and a fix for worktree subagents running git against the wrong repo.
items.key_fact: v2.1.208–210: screen reader mode, vim insert-mode remaps, elapsed-time counter, worktree git fix

items.title: openai-node v6.47.0 Adds Async Iterators and Web Streams Support
items.angle: Two new streaming primitives — async event iterators and fromReadableStream — make it significantly easier to build streaming UIs that compose with the Web Streams API.
items.key_fact: Async event iterators + fromReadableStream for ResponseStream

items.title: Agnost AI (YC S26) Extracts Structured Feedback From Agent Conversations
items.angle: As more products ship agentic features, understanding what users actually say to your agents is a real analytics blind spot — Agnost automates that extraction.
items.key_fact: YC S26 batch; structured feedback extraction from agent conversation logs

items.title: How to Stop Claude From Saying 'Load-Bearing' (and Other Verbal Tics)
items.angle: A practical guide with 408 HN upvotes — the broader lesson is that LLM output style is a controllable parameter if you know which system prompt levers to pull.
items.key_fact: 408 HN upvotes; uses system prompts and style instructions to control Claude's verbal patterns

items.title: Gwern's 'Guardian Angels': A Personal LLM That Mediates All Your Digital Interactions
items.angle: Gwern proposes a deeply researched architecture where a personal LLM agent sits between you and every digital interaction, optimizing for productivity and security simultaneously.
items.key_fact: Full design document from Gwern; personal LLM mediating all digital interactions

items.title: Ternary-Bonsai-27B: A 1.58-Bit Model That's Actually Usable
items.angle: A 27B model quantized to ternary precision that still performs — pushing the boundary of how small you can make a model before it breaks, with direct implications for running large models on edge devices.

items.title: Flawless: An AI SRE Agent That Diagnoses and Remediates Kubernetes Issues
items.angle: Trending at 616 stars, this autonomous SRE agent handles K8s diagnosis and remediation — compare with existing AI ops tools if you're evaluating this space.
items.key_fact: 616 GitHub stars; autonomous Kubernetes diagnosis and remediation

items.title: Juggler: Open-Source GUI Coding Agent From the Creator of JUCE
items.angle: The creator of JUCE — the dominant C++ audio framework — brings a framework builder's sensibility to the GUI coding agent problem. The pedigree suggests this is worth watching.
items.key_fact: Open-source; built by JUCE creator; 163 HN upvotes

items.title: J-Wash: Make Anthropic's Jacobian Lens Interpretability Research Actually Usable
items.angle: Built on Anthropic's Jacobian Lens research, this framework lets you analyze and modify LLM internal representations with exportable results — turning a research paper into a practical tool.
items.key_fact: 139 GitHub stars; exports analysis results; built on Anthropic's interpretability work
